findings.where: hero product mock (sidebar) and Slack thread mock
findings.evidence: focus.json stops 12-22 are the mock's sidebar buttons ('Linear', 'Pulse', 'Inbox', 'My issues', 'Reviews', 'Initiatives', 'Projects', 'Faster app launch', 'Agent tasks', 'Agent Insights', 'UI Refresh'), and stops 25-26 are 'Send message' / 'Schedule for later' in the Slack illustration. A keyboard user tabs through 13 controls of a picture before reaching real content.
findings.before: Illustration rendered as live <button>s in tab order
findings.after: Add inert (or tabindex="-1" plus aria-hidden="true") to the mock containers and give each a short text description (role="img" aria-label="Linear issue view showing...").
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.3 Focus Order and 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the buttons announce as operable but do nothing meaningful.

findings.evidence: dom-1440 headings read 'Intakeand integrations', 'Planningand monitoring', 'AI andautomations', 'Build, review,and ship': the visual line break is made with block spans and no space, so the accessible text runs words together.
findings.after:
Intake and integrations

(a real space or
between the spans)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels: heading navigation reads garbled names.

findings.evidence: dom-1440 records the h1 with empty text; the visible title is built from per-line spans with hide-mobile/show variants (sweep phone_parity points at span.hide-mobile.QI8oKG_titleLine). If the visible spans are aria-hidden duplicates, the h1 name may be empty or doubled.
findings.after:
The product development system for teams and agents

with line breaks done in CSS, or one sr-only copy and aria-hidden on the visual lines.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 and 2.4.6. Confidence low: needs an accessibility-tree check.

findings.evidence: Ten disclosure buttons whose names include the '+' glyph ('Linear Agent +'); the state (open or closed) is only shown by that glyph in the tiles.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value: the expanded state must be programmatic, and the glyph should not be part of the name.

strengths: Skip link is the first focus stop ('Skip to content →'); nav controls have clear names ('Navigate to home').
Body text greys hold contrast on the dark ground outside the mocks; real customer logos.
lang=en, main, header and footer landmarks present.
not_investigated: Sweep contrast hits inside the product mock ('Workspace', 'Favorites' 1.86:1; activity lines 2.21:1) are real for the pixels but sit inside an illustration; if the mock is made inert and described (finding 1) they become decorative.
Product and Resources menus: no live keyboard test of open/close and Escape.
